questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop a short distance away to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is clean.
Add air to the new tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop shortly after to check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them:
questions.explanation: Brakes that pull to one side are a sign of brake problems and need to be checked.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Packed snow reduces traction. Reduce your speed by half or more when driving on packed snow.

questions.question: To leave a parking spot easily, park so you can:

options.text: Park only on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous and should be avoided. Park in a spot where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: Once cargo is secured on a vehicle:

options.text: You do not need to check it.
You should not allow others to inspect it.
You should check it every 150 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check it every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before the trip starts, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should move no more than:
questions.explanation: Pull the slack adjusters to check that they do not move more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: Tires on a commercial truck (not on the front) must have a tread depth of at least:
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 of an inch tread depth. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch tread depth.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to function.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
Hold air only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air for the brakes to work several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used for:

options.text: Making the air brakes work better.
Charging the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if low air pressure has activated them. Pressing the correct control releases the spring brakes for a short time. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tires should be checked regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
The tread wears down faster than in cool weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature. Pay close attention to tire pressure and condition when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: The main cause of death and injury in work zones is:
questions.explanation: The leading cause of death and injury in work zones is drivers going too fast. Slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: The tire load rating is stated:

options.text: On the side of the tire.
On the inside of the tire.
On the inside of the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of the tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load rating, which shows the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure, is written on the side of each tire.

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle with a distracted driver, you should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space and maintain a safe following distance.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Can be used on rear tires.
Can be used if carrying a light load.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: Your wheel bearing seals should be:
questions.explanation: During an inspection, check that wheel bearing seals are not leaking.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful because you cannot control things far away.
Helpful so you can spot hazards early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helpful so you can spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This helps you identify hazards early when you have time to respond.

questions.question: When driving, knowing what is behind you is:
questions.explanation: To drive safely, you must know what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Use your mirrors often to stay aware of your surroundings.
